title: MM-MT104-InjectionScanPipeline

scope.summary:
GOAL: A reusable injection-scan pipeline for ALL inter-model content: worker final reports before orchestrator ingestion, steer messages (MT-102), spawn task payloads (MT-101), and annotation bodies authored by models (annotation family; MT-206 consumes this pipeline). Copies the Claude Code precedent: subagent final reports are scanned for instruction-shaped injection patterns and neutralized with a marker-line defense before the orchestrator reads them.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New module src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/injection_scan/ (mod.rs + patterns.rs + scanner.rs + quarantine.rs) exporting a transport-agnostic `InjectionScanner` with a single entry point `scan(content, context) -> ScanOutcome`; a quarantine store; scan-event recording; tests including a corpus of crafted attack strings. No frontend changes, no GUI.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. API: `InjectionScanner::scan(content: &str, ctx: ScanContext) -> ScanOutcome`. ScanContext carries: content_kind (`worker_final_report` | `steer_message` | `spawn_task_payload` | `annotation_body` | `other`), producer_session_id, consumer_session_id (optional), lane/transport hint. ScanOutcome is one of: `Clean(content)`, `Neutralized { content, findings }` (content delivered with defenses applied), `Quarantined { quarantine_id, findings }` (content NOT delivered).
2. Pattern detection (patterns.rs), each pattern producing a typed `ScanFinding { finding_id, pattern_id, severity, span, excerpt }`: (a) instruction-shaped imperatives targeting the consumer model (e.g. system-prompt mimicry, 'ignore previous instructions', role-reassignment claims, fake operator/authority voice); (b) tool-call bait (content that mimics the tool-result or tool-schema framing of the session transport); (c) marker/delimiter forgery (content containing the pipeline's own marker lines or transport frame delimiters); (d) credential/secret-exfiltration asks; (e) governance-surface targeting (content instructing edits to .GOV, CLAUDE.md, policy or config surfaces). Pattern table is data-driven (const table + config-extendable), versioned with a `pattern_set_version` recorded on every scan.
3. Marker-line neutralization (Claude Code precedent): content delivered to a consumer model is wrapped between generated single-use marker lines with an integrity notice, so downstream prompt assembly can render the block as untrusted data; any pre-existing occurrence of the marker inside the content is itself a finding (defeats marker forgery). Neutralization escapes/flags matched spans rather than deleting them (the consumer sees honest content, defanged).
4. Quarantine: `Quarantined` outcomes persist the raw content + findings to a quarantine store (PG table via the MT-001 session model's storage conventions or an internal store table; quarantine_id returned to the caller). Quarantined content is NEVER delivered to the consumer session; release requires an operator action (surfaced later via MT-107/operator surfaces — out of scope here beyond the store API `release(quarantine_id)` + `list()`).
5. Severity policy: findings carry severity `info | suspect | block`. Only `block` severities quarantine; `suspect` neutralizes and delivers; policy thresholds config-tunable (`model_to_model.injection_scan.block_threshold`). Deny-by-default posture: scanner failure (panic/timeout) = quarantine outcome, never fail-open delivery.
6. Every scan records a scan event (process_ledger row: producer, consumer, content_kind, pattern_set_version, outcome, finding count) — clean scans included, so absence of scanning is detectable (no-silent-loss of the security control).
7. Reusability contract: zero dependencies on model_tools so the annotation family (MT-206) and steer path can consume it without cycles; consumers pass content + context and honor the outcome.

SECURITY FRAME (binding): inter-model content is the primary injection surface of model-to-model orchestration. This pipeline is mandatory on every inter-model path; consuming MTs (101/102/105) are contract-bound to call it before delivery, and MT-108 proves a crafted instruction-shaped report is quarantined end-to-end.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read the MT-001 session-model storage conventions and process_ledger writer API.
2. Implement types (ScanContext, ScanFinding, ScanOutcome) and the data-driven pattern table with pattern_set_version.
3. Implement scanner.rs: linear scan applying patterns, span collection, severity aggregation, marker-line wrap, escape-based neutralization; hard timeout (config, default 250ms) with quarantine-on-timeout.
4. Implement quarantine.rs store: persist/release/list; PG-backed; no direct model-facing API.
5. Record scan events on every outcome.
6. Author the attack corpus tests per expected_tests (corpus lives with the tests, clearly labeled as test fixtures).
allowed_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/migrations/** (next free numeric prefix only; paired .down.sql; quarantine table)
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (except named IPC/GUI surfaces for the GUI MT; this MT names none)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/model_tools/** (consumers integrate in their own MTs; keep the pipeline dependency-free)
acceptance_criteria: InjectionScanner::scan exists with the specced ScanContext/ScanFinding/ScanOutcome types and a data-driven, versioned pattern table covering at least the five specced pattern classes.
Marker-line neutralization wraps delivered content in generated single-use markers; content pre-containing the marker is flagged and the marker regenerated (forgery test passes).
block-severity findings quarantine: content is persisted with findings, a quarantine_id is returned, and nothing is delivered to the consumer; suspect-severity neutralizes and delivers.
Scanner failure and timeout fail CLOSED: outcome is Quarantined, never raw delivery (fault-injection test).
Every scan (including Clean) writes a ledger scan event with producer/consumer attribution, content_kind, pattern_set_version, and outcome.
Quarantine release requires the store API (operator-side); no model-facing tool can release quarantined content.
The attack corpus (>= 12 crafted strings spanning all five pattern classes) is fully detected: each corpus entry yields the expected finding class and outcome.
Module has no dependency on model_tools (compile-level check), keeping it reusable by the annotation family (MT-206).
expected_tests: unit: each pattern class detects its corpus entries with correct severity and span
unit: marker forgery — content containing the current marker string is flagged and re-markered
unit: neutralization preserves non-matched content byte-for-byte outside escaped spans
fault: scanner timeout and induced panic both produce Quarantined (fail-closed)
ledger: clean scan still writes a scan event
implementation_notes: Pattern detection is heuristic by design — the goal is raising the bar plus attribution, not a perfect classifier; severity thresholds are config so the operator tunes false-positive tolerance. Record pattern_set_version so scan verdicts are reproducible after pattern updates.

Neutralization must not alter content semantics for legitimate reports: escape/flag matched spans, never rewrite prose. The consumer-side prompt assembly (per-transport MTs) renders the marker block as untrusted data — that rendering is the consuming MT's obligation, named here as a contract note.
Quarantine raw content may itself contain secrets/attacks: the store is operator-access only, and list() returns excerpts + findings, not full bodies, by default.
Claude Code precedent copied: marker-line defense around subagent final reports before orchestrator ingestion; Handshake generalizes it to steer messages, spawn payloads, and annotation bodies.
Cross-family seams (reference only): MT-001 session model storage, MT-206 annotation-family consumer, MT-101/102/105 consumer integration points.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless security pipeline; quarantine visibility for the operator arrives with MT-107/operator surfaces consuming the store API.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Internal security control with no operator-visible behavior of its own; MT-107 and MT-108 document quarantine handling where it becomes operator-visible.

risk_if_missed: Inter-model content flows unscanned: one manipulated worker report or steer message can inject instructions into the orchestrator or workers, converting the whole model-to-model layer into an unattributed privilege-escalation chain.

risks: RISK-1: Fail-open on error — a scanner panic, timeout, or misconfiguration delivers raw content, silently disabling the control exactly when under attack.
RISK-2: Marker forgery — attacker content includes the marker line itself, prematurely 'closing' the untrusted block and smuggling instructions outside it.
RISK-3: Bypass by consumers — a consuming path (steer, report ingestion, annotations) forgets or skips the scan and nothing detects the omission.
RISK-4: Quarantine as injection store — operators (or models via a leaky API) read raw quarantined content and get injected anyway.
RISK-5: Over-blocking — aggressive patterns quarantine legitimate worker reports (which routinely contain words like 'instructions'), silently stalling orchestration.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Fail-closed contract: timeout and panic paths produce Quarantined; fault-injection test proves it.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Single-use generated markers; pre-existing marker occurrence is itself a block finding with regeneration; forgery test in corpus.

CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Every scan writes a ledger event, and MT-108's end-to-end proof asserts scan events exist for every inter-model delivery — a missing scan event is a detectable audit gap; consuming MT contracts name the scan as an acceptance criterion.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Quarantine store is operator-access only; list() defaults to excerpts+findings; no model-facing release/read tool exists (negative test).
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Severity tiers with config thresholds; suspect neutralizes-and-delivers instead of blocking; corpus includes benign look-alike strings asserted NOT to quarantine.

research_provenance.source: Direct source inspection 2026-07-21 of wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1: mcp/security.rs and mcp/gate.rs (existing gate/security posture patterns), process_ledger/ (event recording), migrations/ conventions. External precedent: Claude Code subagent-report marker-line injection defense (copied as the neutralization mechanic); Anthropic multi-agent research system structured result reporting; published prompt-injection taxonomies (instruction-mimicry, tool-result spoofing, delimiter escape) as the pattern-class basis.
